problem:
Given that 
$|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a & b+2\end{aligned}|=8$,
find 
$|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a+3 & b\end{aligned}|.$

feedback.worked_solution:
We "factor out" the given determinant from the determinant we would like to find:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}a+2 & -5 \\ b+4 & 6\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}(a+3)-1 & -5 \\ b+4 & 6\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}(a+3)-1 & -5 \\ b+4 & 6\end{aligned}| & ={{|\begin{aligned}a+3 & -5 \\ b & 6\end{aligned}|}_{⏟}}_{-7}+|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =-7+(-6+20) \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
